name: Canaria-Systems-S1-streaming-compact-runtime-v1
question: Can direct streaming execution of a compact low-rank functional representation reduce peak resident model memory relative to full dense materialization while preserving the represented function?
environment_policy: Record the exact runtime used. This exploratory systems result is environment-specific; do not generalize hardware performance.

operator.form: x <- x + alpha * (x @ U) @ V; dense equivalent W = U @ V and x <- x + alpha * x @ W

modes: dense_resident: load all 32 expanded W matrices before inference
dense_streaming: memory-map one expanded W at a time, execute, release
factor_streaming: memory-map one compact U,V pair at a time and execute directly without constructing W

capacity_witness.interpretation: A logical model-payload budget only; not an OS-enforced RAM limit. dense_resident must exceed it and factor_streaming peak model payload must fit below it.

pass_rule: factor_streaming peak model payload <= 0.20 * dense_resident peak model payload
factor_streaming measured peak RSS delta < dense_resident measured peak RSS delta
factor_streaming output passes both locked float32 tolerances against dense_resident
dense_streaming output passes locked max-abs tolerance against dense_resident
dense_resident model payload exceeds 32 MiB capacity witness while factor_streaming peak model payload is below it
boundaries: This does not show that arbitrary trained neural operators admit the low-rank representation.
This does not establish MCU, GPU, mobile, browser, or general edge deployment.
This does not strengthen the scientific compositional-simplification claim.
Measured latency is secondary and hardware/runtime-specific.
A later experiment must connect an actually learned Canaria replacement to a streaming runtime before making deployment claims.
